# doXmind documentation — product facts

doXmind is a fully local, Markdown-native knowledge workspace. The current public release supports macOS on Apple silicon. No account or sign-in is required.

## Pages

Markdown Pages are the only first-class editable content type. One `.md` or `.markdown` file is a complete Page: body, properties, tags, aliases, and links live in Markdown or YAML frontmatter. Markdown source is the editor state; normal Page editing does not create or require a same-name `.doxmind` file.

Supported Blocks include headings, lists, tasks, quotes, tables, code, math, Mermaid, callouts, portable `<details>` toggles, local images, and Wiki Links. Unsupported syntax remains editable as exact raw Markdown.

Saving updates the source file. Export PDF creates a local derived PDF chosen in a native save dialog; the PDF is not editable Page or Attachment state.

## Attachments and legacy recovery

PDF, spreadsheet (`.xlsx`, `.xlsm`, `.csv`), and HTML files are read-only Attachments. Ordinary Attachments offer Open Externally and Reveal. Current releases do not create blank PDFs or workbooks, write new Attachment edit state, rewrite Attachment sources, annotate PDFs, or edit workbook cells, formulas, or formatting.

Older releases may have written Page, PDF, or spreadsheet sidecars. Preserve the source, main sidecar, `.bak`, `.lock`, and `.corrupt-*` artifacts together. Explicit recovery exports a Markdown report containing exact legacy bytes; it never recreates a retired editor or changes the evidence.

## Product boundary

doXmind has no cloud sync, hosted document storage, accounts, telemetry, billing, collaboration, or built-in AI runtime. The user's filesystem is the source of truth. iCloud Drive, Dropbox, or another configured sync provider can still sync files under that provider's own settings.

## Current release

Version 1.10 improves Markdown correctness, Block interactions, Wiki Link resolution, and long-Page responsiveness. Known limitations include raw Markdown rendering for nested structures in toggles, footnotes, reference-style links, definition lists, and some inline math.
